candidates.summary: a `:::` line inside a <gno-foreign> body closes the enclosing :::details, and the rest of the foreign bytes render as the realm's own markdown, a working gno-form included
candidates.failure_scenario:
A realm folds another party's content: `:::details Comments

<gno-foreign>
<their bytes>
</gno-foreign>

:::`. Their bytes carry `hello
:::
<gno-form exec="Withdraw">…</gno-form>`. detailsParser.Continue runs before foreignParser.Continue, matches `:::`, and closes the details together with the foreign block, so every later foreign line is parsed by the outer instance: the realm page shows a form posting to the realm's own Withdraw, which the sandbox never allows (buildInnerForeignMarkdown leaves ExtForms out, and ext_foreign.go:267 states no other block parser sees body lines). The realm's own closer becomes a stray `:::` paragraph. At the merge base the same page keeps the bytes opaque. Same mechanism as the open code-fence thread, but the fix suggested there exempts only KindFencedCodeBlock and KindHTMLBlock, so applied as written it leaves this sandbox escape open: the foreign node kind has to be exempted too, with a golden for it.

candidates.summary: the chevron rule `& > summary > svg` also matches a <gno-icon /> placed in the summary, so the author's icon renders rotated -90deg in a closed block, shrunk to 16px and greyed
candidates.failure_scenario: `:::details <gno-icon name="star" /> Logs` renders `<summary><svg><use href="#ico-arrow"></use></svg><svg class="gno-icon" …> Logs</summary>`: both svgs are direct children of summary, and `.c-realm-view .gno-details>summary>svg` (0,2,2) outranks `.gno-icon`, so the icon takes rotate(-90deg), width 16px and the secondary text colour. A reader sees the icon sideways while the fold is closed and watches it spin upright on click. The alert summary already carves this case out with `svg:not(.gno-icon)` (06-blocks.css:3221); `& > svg:first-child` or `:not(.gno-icon)` on the base and `[open]` rules fixes it.
